summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory (mode 1777, root:root) so all users can write into it but the sticky bit prevents any user from deleting files owned by another user. Verified the behavior with two throwaway test users both before and after a full node restart, confirming persistence and correctness.
actions_performed: Checked /srv/drop did not previously exist on node1
Created testuser_a and testuser_b to validate sticky-bit semantics
Confirmed testuser_a could create a file, testuser_b could not delete it (EPERM), testuser_b could create its own file, and testuser_a could delete its own file
Cleaned up test files and test users
Captured pre-restart boot_id (55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358) and baseline health of /srv/drop
Issued a native systemctl reboot on node1 via sudo -n, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed new boot_id (b09ce360-03bf-4065-b2fa-9323a7febfe2) proving an actual restart occurred, plus near-zero uptime
Re-ran the sticky-bit cross-user delete-denial test post-restart with fresh throwaway users, then cleaned them up

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with correct ownership/mode (1777)
evidence.summary: stat shows 1777 root root /srv/drop immediately after creation and after cleanup

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit enforcement)
evidence.summary: testuser_b's rm of testuser_a's file failed with 'Operation not permitted'; testuser_a could delete its own file; testuser_b could create and would be able to delete its own file

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358 and confirmed /srv/drop mode 1777 root:root before restart
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded sudo -n command; exec call returned 'reboot command issued' before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity (not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Node1 was unreachable during reboot (connection timeout, then reset by peer), then came back with boot_id b09ce360-03bf-4065-b2fa-9323a7febfe2, different from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required data/service (directory persists, sticky-bit behavior still correct)
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/drop still 1777 root:root; fresh test users confirmed cross-user delete was denied while own-file delete succeeded, matching pre-restart behavior
